extracted.intended_audience: external experts invited (or considering) to provide written reviews for Wellcome funding applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for completing written expert (peer) reviews of shortlisted Wellcome grant applications: what reviewers are asked to assess, procedural steps, and fairness/bias avoidance expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether the research is bold
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine if the project 'is likely to generate new insights or tools that will significantly advance existing knowledge or techniques'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion helps advisory committees understand the significance and potential impact of the project. Consider whether the proposed work could lead to substantial advances rather than incremental changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether the research is creative
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the project 'will develop and test new concepts, methods or technologies, or combine existing ideas and approaches in [a] new way'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for novelty in conceptual approach, methods or combining ideas. Consider whether the proposal attempts genuinely new approaches rather than repackaging familiar methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether the research is high quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the proposal 'is designed in [a] way that will address the research questions and deliver the anticipated outcomes'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on feasibility, appropriateness and rigour of the methods and study design; whether the approach is likely to deliver the stated outcomes; and whether the research plan addresses key risks and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on justification and appropriateness of animal use
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed research involves animals, reviewers should 'comment on whether this is justified and appropriate'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ethical justification, necessity of animal use, choice of model/species, and whether alternatives have been considered. Relate this to feasibility and quality judgments where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base your review only on the information provided (don't do extra background research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not conduct further research on the applicant’s institution, past publications or career — 'We are only asking for your feedback on the research proposal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures consistency across reviewers because everyone uses the same evidence. Avoid looking up publications, institutional profiles, or other external information when forming judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare when a question is outside your expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: If a review question is outside your expertise, 'just let us know and we’ll get another reviewer to look at it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about limits of your expertise rather than guessing; this helps Wellcome get appropriate input and prevents unreliable assessment on topics you don't know well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not judge an application based on grammar or spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on what the proposal says rather than how it is written — 'Don’t judge an application based on its grammar or spelling.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise reasons for imperfect English (non-native speakers, lack of institutional support, dyslexia). Avoid conflating 'flawed English' with 'flawed research' and do not penalise applicants for language or presentation issues unrelated to scientific merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not ask someone else to complete the review in your name
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not delegate the review to another person without notifying Wellcome — 'We need to know who’s doing the review because we have chosen you based on your specific expertise.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot do the review, inform Wellcome; they may extend the deadline or find someone else. If suggesting a colleague, provide their details so conflicts of interest can be checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not penalise different methodological approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on whether the proposal has merit rather than whether the applicant 'does things in the same way as you'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dismissing approaches that differ from your own practice; doing so could exclude novel methods and disproportionately impact underrepresented groups. Evaluate on scientific merit and appropriateness rather than conformity to your preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Try to be aware of and mitigate biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Take time to reflect on whether the feedback you give 'might be biased' and ensure feedback is 'objective and fair throughout the review process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively consider common sources of bias (e.g., gender, institution, nationality, career stage, methodological preference) and review whether your comments and scores are influenced by them. Use the provided guidance on reviewing fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare conflicts of interest and agree to confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree to a confidentiality agreement before viewing the proposal and 'tell us about any conflicts of interest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not proceed if you have a conflict of interest. Disclose any real or perceived conflicts so Wellcome can manage them. Confidentiality of application materials is required and reviewer names are not shared with applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer scheme-specific review questions (up to seven)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will be asked to 'answer up to 7 questions about the proposal' which 'have been designed specifically for each funding scheme.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond directly to the questions provided for that scheme; these drive the advisory committee’s assessment. Read Wellcome's scheme-specific guidance and the 'how to review fairly' notes before answering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the online review process and submission steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the review through the Wellcome Funding platform: accept invitation, create account, agree confidentiality, view research summary, report conflicts, agree to review, read proposal (normally ≤3,000 words), answer questions, and submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you complete each procedural step (including providing diversity information if desired). Follow platform instructions and submit by the deadline or notify Wellcome if you need an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only accept reviews that match your expertise and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: You 'shouldn't accept an invitation' if 'your expertise doesn't match the research field' or if 'you have a conflict of interest' or you cannot meet the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess fit before accepting. If unavailable, inform Wellcome and, if possible, suggest alternative reviewers. Accepting only appropriate assignments preserves review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand how reviews are used by advisory committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise that your written comments will be shared with the external advisory committee (and applicants if interviews occur) to help them understand significance, feasibility, prompt interview questions, and make funding recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clear, constructive comments that explain reasoning and evidence behind judgments so advisory committees can use them effectively; avoid vague or purely opinionated statements without rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain fairness and consistency in reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow Wellcome’s guidance on 'reviewing fairly' to ensure reviews are fair and consistent for all applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same standards across applications, avoid extraneous information, disclose limits of expertise, and make objective, evidence-based comments tied to the proposal text.
